qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care vocabulary: words naming the field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychologist, psychology, 'mental health') and words for talking-cure care (therapy, talk therapy, counselling, sharing feelings in group sessions). Plain diagnoses (depression, anxiety) and therapy acronyms (CBT) stay low. Known side channel: the word ' talking' even outside care (a talking parrot ~0.3); ordinary medical scenes hum at 0.1-0.4, so it is a weak preference, not a clean switch.

fire: The talking parrot repeated every word the sailor said.
After months of sleepless nights, she finally booked an appointment with a psychiatrist.
He studied psychology at university before training as a clinical psychologist.
The school hired two counsellors to support students' mental health during exam season.
Talk therapy helped him understand why he kept pushing people away.
Every Tuesday the group met in a circle, sharing their feelings about grief and loss.
The hospital opened a new psychiatric ward with twenty beds.
Her insurance finally covered weekly therapy sessions with a licensed therapist.
quiet: Asthma can be helped by inhalers and steroid tablets.
After months of sleepless nights, she finally bought a new mattress and blackout curtains.
He studied geology at university before working as a field surveyor.
The school hired two coaches to support students' fitness during the football season.
Long walks helped him clear his head after work on Fridays.
Every Tuesday the group met in a circle, knitting scarves for the winter fair.
The hospital opened a new maternity ward with twenty beds.
Her insurance finally covered the dental crown on her back molar.

predictions: Blind test (label-only second author). Expect care-word fires around 0.3-0.5 and most near misses below 0.2; the asthma leak (~0.29) and the parrot fire (~0.29) sit near the bars, so the margin is thin.
